description:
The application window is expected to close on: 09/17/2026
Job posting may be removed earlier if the position is filled or if a sufficient number of applications are received.

This position is remote, preference will be given to candidates in the western region of the United States.
 

Meet the Team

The Strategic Program Management team partners with leaders across Cisco to deliver the organization’s most meaningful and ambiguous priorities. We build operating mechanisms that make execution more predictable, scalable, and repeatable: coordinated plans, process forums, decision logs, shared metrics, risk and dependency management, and concise leadership reporting. Reporting to the Director of Strategy & Planning, you will join a team that values practical problem-solving, strong partnership, focused execution, and growth driver outcomes.

Your Impact

As a Senior Strategy & Planning Program Manager, you will lead high-priority, complex initiatives that span products, architectures, go-to-market, operations, and customer outcomes. These programs often begin with an understood destination but an unclear path: ownership, dependencies, decisions, measures, and operating mechanisms must be defined and aligned.

You will serve as the connective execution layer across the organization—turning strategy into actionable, governed programs. You will not own product strategy, technical design, engineering delivery, or commercial decisions; instead, you will enable accountable leaders to make timely decisions and execute effectively through coordinated planning, governance, risk management, and clear executive visibility.   In this role, you will:

Lead strategic, cross-functional programs from initial framing through execution, transition, and closeout.

Translate ambiguous objectives into a clear program structure: outcomes, scope, workstreams, sponsorship, measures, dependencies, decision rights, and path to delivery.

Develop integrated execution plans that connect teams, milestones, assumptions, risks, and commitments across organizational boundaries.

Establish processes and operating rhythms that accelerate decisions, surface tradeoffs early, and maintain accountability through delivery.

Provide senior leaders with concise, decision-oriented visibility into program health, progress, risks, dependencies, and actions required.

Improve execution systems and operating mechanisms so teams spend less time on manual coordination and reporting, and more time delivering strategic outcomes.

Capture lessons learned, reusable templates, and scalable practices that strengthen future programs.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelors + 12 years of related experience, or​ Masters + 8 years of related experience, or ​ PhD + 5 years of related experience, or ​ equivalent relevant work experience​

6+ years of experience leading complex strategic programs, business planning initiatives, business operations, or product/go-to-market operations. 

4+ years leading large, cross-functional initiatives in an operations-focused environment.

Experience building integrated plans, executive governance, operating cadences, performance metrics, and risk/dependency management processes.

Preferred Qualifications

Exceptional communication and influence skills, including the ability to engage senior leaders, align diverse stakeholders, and drive decisions without direct authority.

Strong analytical judgment and ability to turn complex information into clear recommendations, tradeoffs, and executive-ready updates.

Experience in enterprise technology, SaaS, product management, product operations, go-to-market execution, or customer lifecycle programs.

Familiarity with product lifecycle motions, including launches, refreshes, migrations, End-of-Sale, and End-of-Life.

Experience working across product, engineering, sales, finance, customer success, and operations organizations.

Experience with portfolio management, financial analysis, dashboards, CRM/reporting tools, and program-management methodologies.

PMP, Agile, Scrum, or comparable program-management certification.

 

Why Cisco? 

At Cisco, we’re revolutionizing how data and infrastructure connect and protect organizations in the AI era – and beyond. We’ve been innovating fearlessly for 40 years to create solutions that power how humans and technology work together across the physical and digital worlds. These solutions provide customers with unparalleled security, visibility, and insights across the entire digital footprint.

Fueled by the depth and breadth of our technology, we experiment and create meaningful solutions. Add to that our worldwide network of doers and experts, and you’ll see that the opportunities to grow and build are limitless. We work as a team, collaborating with empathy to make really big things happen on a global scale. Because our solutions are everywhere, our impact is everywhere. 

We are Cisco, and our power starts with you.

U.S. employees are eligible for paid time away as described below, subject to Cisco’s policies:

10 paid holidays per full calendar year, plus 1 floating holiday for non-exempt employees

1 paid day off for employee’s birthday, paid year-end holiday shutdown, and 4 paid days off for personal wellness determined by Cisco

Non-exempt employees** receive 16 days of paid vacation time per full calendar year, accrued at rate of 4.92 hours per pay period for full-time employees

Exempt employees participate in Cisco’s flexible vacation time off program, which has no defined limit on how much vacation time eligible employees may use (subject to availability and some business limitations)

80 hours of sick time off provided on hire date and each January 1st thereafter, and up to 80 hours of unused sick time carried forward from one calendar year to the next

Additional paid time away may be requested to deal with critical or emergency issues for family members

Optional 10 paid days per full calendar year to volunteer

For non-sales roles, employees are also eligible to earn annual bonuses subject to Cisco’s policies.

Employees on sales plans earn performance-based incentive pay on top of their base salary, which is split between quota and non-quota components, subject to the applicable Cisco plan. For quota-based incentive pay, Cisco typically pays as follows:

.75% of incentive target for each 1% of revenue attainment up to 50% of quota;

1.5% of incentive target for each 1% of attainment between 50% and 75%;

1% of incentive target for each 1% of attainment between 75% and 100%; and

Once performance exceeds 100% attainment, incentive rates are at or above 1% for each 1% of attainment with no cap on incentive compensation.

For non-quota-based sales performance elements such as strategic sales objectives, Cisco may pay 0% up to 125% of target. Cisco sales plans do not have a minimum threshold of performance for sales incentive compensation to be paid.
